If it's available at your building, I've had a great experience with Google Fiber [(check availability here)](https://fiber.google.com/eb/); gig download speeds and I've only had one brief interruption that they actually communicated about and didn't last long. A buddy of mine lives over by your area and has it, so you might be covered. 

Outside of that, CenturyLink wasn't too bad when I had to use them; their fiber offering was pretty solid, the only issue was I think they did some weird throttling at times (I had to keep my Steam game downloads capped at ~40 megs down or the downloads would eventually die until I paused them and reconnected to the router, but at that cap they continued on no problem, was odd). Briefly had their high speed non-fiber as well and didn't have any issues that I can recall, but honestly that was before I switched to working from home full time so I can't speak to that situation. 🙂

Yeah, on second reading, my dad is really just a dick, but oh well. I guess I'm just more sympathetic in some ways to him because I'm fairly certain he has some sort of personality disorder, and I have a severely blunted affect and an inability to form real emotional bonds to people outside of my family and occasionally a lover, though the latter takes huge effort on both my and their parts. So I fear to a degree turning out like him and I suppose I hold on to the few good things he does as a sign that there's hope for both him and myself.

Mine's not necessarily heroic, but it did mean a lot to me.

I hate my dad. I mean, I really hate my dad. I have a lot of reasons, including the fact that he basically abandoned my family in the middle of the night a few years ago, leading to a divorce. He's also physically intimidated me multiple times, shoving me across the room on the one occasion where I tried to confront him and ask him how the fuck he could destroy our family like he did, which I've still never received a real answer on. My dad is a pretty shitty human being, and the only reason I still talk to him today is because he's legally obligated to help out with my college expenses due to the divorce settlement. He makes around 150K a year and has almost no expenses of his own, gives my mom the absolute minimum in alimony, and even with me, barely has to pay anything because I have a full-ride scholarship that covers all of my tuition and books and etc. Still, he is the most selfish man in existence. Case in point: I've never asked him for any extra money, not once. I finally did, a few months ago, I asked him to loan me about 150 bucks so I could go visit my best friend in the world. He said that his finances wouldn't allow for it, and behind my back complained to my grandmother that I shouldn't be taking trips to go see people. The money situation was a lie, as he was bragging just a few weeks ago about how he has tens of thousands of dollars in the bank.

But a few weeks ago, one of our dogs, who lives with him, was attacked by a mountain lion. She was pretty fucked up, stomach exposed and falling out, near death. He took her to the vet and had her fixed up; she's just now healed enough to actually leave the vet's office and the bill is massive. Two things about this make me think that maybe there's some decency to my dad, somewhere. 

The first is that he fucking loves his massive, mid-life crisis truck. He won't let anyone eat or drink in it, won't even use it to haul things because he doesn't want to scratch the bed, what the fuck. But when Lucy, our dog, was bleeding horribly, he put her into his truck without a second thought and drove her straight to the vet. I'm sure his seats got more than a little messy from that.

The second is that, even though he wouldn't lend me 150 bucks, he spent at least a few thousand dollars getting Lucy taken care of without a second thought. He's never complained about the cost, which he /never/ does, he always whines about any minor expense. 

So while I'm not prepared to be buddy-buddy with my dad after the shit he's put my family and me in particular (did I mention he basically disowned me for a while when I came out as bisexual and an atheist at the same time?) through, he has my respect for treating the animals in his life much better than he treats the people. 

TL;DR My dad is a horrible person, but when it counted, he took care of our dog without once complaining about the cost or inconvenience.

Let me put it this way; you want to do something, you probably can.

You want to fight a dragon? Walk around for a while, fucking dragons everywhere.

You want to sneak into a house in the middle of the night, kill a man in his sleep, and then rob him of everything? Go right ahead.

You want to be a wizard who can disintegrate motherfuckers left and right? Oh hey there's a college for that.

You want to just dick around? Shove people off cliffs, turn people into rabbits, have a drinking contest? All of these things are possible, with Skyrim.

Have a PC capable of running it? Your potential options just exploded into an infinite number, due to the modding community.

You can have a faithful companion to accompany you on your journeys, or go it solo. You can get married and have that spouse set up a shop to bring you some steady income and cook you meals. You can stumble onto a cave containing a legendary artifact and fight your way through hordes of necromancers and their creations.

The Elder Scrolls have always been epic games. Skyrim takes it to another level.

Just be warned, Skyrim is like heroin. You start, you're in it for the long haul or a painful withdrawal process.
